description: Write a pandas ETL script for insurance_group that builds a golden customer record from three source systems with field-level survivorship rules. Rules: (1) name, email and phone take the first non-empty value in source priority order crm > billing > support, (2) address takes the value from the record with the most recent updated_at among records that have a non-empty address, (3) empty strings and whitespace-only strings count as missing, (4) the output has one row per person_id plus a provenance column recording which source supplied each field.
edge_cases: The crm record is the most recently updated but its address is whitespace only; address must come from billing (latest non-empty)
email is null in crm, so the next priority source (billing) supplies it, not support
Source priority must be an explicit ordering; alphabetical sort (billing < crm < support) gives the wrong winner
groupby().first() skips NaN but not empty strings, so blanks must be converted to NaN first
Input order is arbitrary and must not influence the result
common_failure_modes: FM3: Taking the whole row from the highest-priority or most recent source instead of field-level survivorship loses email and address
FM7: Empty strings treated as valid values override real data from lower-priority sources
FM1: Implicit alphabetical source ordering replaces the business priority
